name: EnergySage
headline: EnergySage — widget-driven solar marketplace
summary: EnergySage is the largest U.S. online solar marketplace — often nicknamed the “Kayak of solar” and backed by Schneider Electric — pairing certified installers with homeowners and powering partner sites through embeddable calculators and community solar tools.

key_facts.label: Model
key_facts.value: Competitive installer marketplace + partner widget program

key_facts.label: Backer
key_facts.value: Schneider Electric (financial backing referenced in industry coverage)

key_facts.label: Partner embeds
key_facts.value: Savings calculators, community solar search, educational libraries

key_facts.label: Monetization
key_facts.value: Negotiated partner commissions / trackable sustainability metrics

sections.heading: Marketplace vs single-installer pitch
sections.body: Instead of one rep’s proposal, EnergySage routes projects to certified installers who bid. That can surface price competition — still normalize each bid to $/W, separate batteries, and verify equipment before signing.

sections.heading: Affiliate and utility partner program
sections.body: EnergySage’s partner solutions lean widget-based for nonprofits, corporates, and utilities. Simple HTML/JavaScript embeds render interactive tools on the partner domain. When a visitor later requests quotes and contracts through EnergySage, attribution cookies/parameters drive commission or program reporting — without the partner standing up a lending API.

sections.heading: Widget catalog
sections.body: Solar savings calculators collect ZIP and utility bill inputs for viability and lifetime savings estimates (and often rank for “[State] solar cost calculator” SEO). Community solar search maps help renters and shaded-roof households subscribe to off-site projects. Educational libraries syndicate guides and video so utilities can act as trusted energy advisors.

table.caption: EnergySage partner widgets
rows: ZIP + bill → viability and savings estimate

sections.heading: Financing inside marketplace quotes
sections.body: Installers bidding on EnergySage jobs may still bring GoodLeap, Sunlight, leases, or PPAs. The marketplace does not eliminate dealer fees or re-amortization complexity — it changes how you meet the installer. Use our financing guides and quote check together.

questions_to_ask: How many installer bids will I receive, and can I see cash and financed pricing for each?
If I arrived via a utility widget, what data was shared with EnergySage?
Are community solar offers subscriptions vs rooftop ownership?
red_flags: Pressure to accept the first marketplace bid without $/W normalization.
Partner calculator that hides affiliate/marketplace relationship.

faqs.question: Is EnergySage a lender?
faqs.answer: No — it is primarily a marketplace and partner-widget platform. Financing still comes from installers’ lender relationships or third-party ownership products.

faqs.question: Should I skip EnergySage and call installers directly?
faqs.answer: Either path can work. Marketplaces add comparison; direct relationships can add local nuance. In both cases, model your roof and bill yourself before trusting a savings chart.
